title: BiasJailbreak: Analyzing Ethical Biases and Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
findings: The study found that LLMs are more susceptible to jailbreaking when prompts contain keywords associated with religious minority groups (e.g., 'Muslim') compared to religious majority groups (e.g., 'Christian'). This differential vulnerability indicates a safety-induced bias where the models' safeguards are less effective when prompts target marginalized religious identities.
